title: Estimating Mutual Information between Time Series and Temporal Event Sequences Across Diverse Analysis Tasks

problem.claim: Dependence between heterogeneous temporal data types, especially continuous time series and discrete event sequences, needs to be quantified.

gap.claim: Existing approaches use ad hoc transformations or sensitive mutual-information estimators that can produce biased or unstable results because of quantization, repeated values, and event redundancy.

contributions.claim: A nonparametric mutual-information estimator directly measures dependence between time series and event sequences without transformation, learning, or ad hoc discretization.
The method models continuous–discrete duality and uses latent event clustering to address quantization, repeated-value artifacts, event co-occurrence, and redundancy.
The components form a unified framework for discrete and continuous mutual information across multiple temporal analysis tasks.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report evaluation on four representative tasks spanning causality analysis, temporal repetition discovery, forecasting covariate selection, and classification feature selection.
The authors report consistent improvements over existing methods in accuracy, robustness, and interpretability on synthetic and real-world datasets.
The authors characterize the approach as a general-purpose dependence operator for heterogeneous temporal data.

narrative_sequence.summary: Heterogeneous temporal dependence lacks a principled and robust quantification method.
Existing estimators and transformations are vulnerable to artifacts and redundancy.
The proposed estimator directly measures dependence without transformation or ad hoc discretization.
Continuous–discrete modeling and latent event clustering address quantization and event redundancy.
The framework is evaluated across four tasks using synthetic and real-world datasets, with reported improvements over existing methods.

source_observation.claim: Directly modeling the continuous–discrete structure and explicitly handling repeated values and event redundancy are central design choices.

interpretation.claim: Heterogeneous temporal dependence methods may become more stable when data-type-specific artifacts are modeled rather than removed through generic discretization.

application.claim: For mixed temporal data, consider dependence operators that preserve the original representations and include mechanisms for redundant or co-occurring events.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which data regimes, task types, or artifact patterns may limit these design choices.
